Trump administration ties bid to block Alaska Senate certification to second Sullivan

Reuters

30 October, 2026 03:30 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Jacob Bogage, Luc Cohen and Bo Erickson ROCK HILL, South Carolina, Oct 29 (Reuters) – The US Justice Department filed a revised lawsuit on Thursday seeking to block certification of Alaska’s election results if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan loses narrowly, citing a New York Times report that Democratic operatives recruited a candidate with the same first and last names.

The suit raises the prospect of a messy fight over a contest that could determine Senate control in next Tuesday’s midterm elections.

Alaska is one of about 10 highly competitive races that will decide control of the Senate, where Republicans hold a 53-47 majority. Democrats need a net gain of four seats, and a post-election dispute in Alaska could leave control of the chamber unclear for weeks.

Show Full Article

Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy also called for a state investigation into the allegations, after the Times reported that aides to Democratic candidate Mary Peltola worked to recruit two candidates who could siphon votes from the incumbent Senator Sullivan.

“They orchestrated his sham campaign for the purpose of misleading Alaskan voters and getting Peltola elected,” lawyers for the Justice Department wrote in their amended complaint, citing the Times report.

Peltola’s campaign and its lawyers did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the Justice Department’s amended complaint.

Reuters has not verified the New York Times report.

Trump for years has sowed doubts about the fairness of US elections and even prior to the Times report had pushed the Justice Department to file a lawsuit seeking to preemptively block Alaska from certifying Peltola, a former congresswoman, if she were to win the election.

WAVE OF SUBPOENAS

The Justice Department issued more than 40 subpoenas and document preservation requests in its probe, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday.

President Donald Trump told reporters earlier on Thursday: “It’s hard to believe that she could even be allowed to run. Frankly, I don’t know how you can allow somebody like that to run. It’s so unfair.”

As campaigning enters its final few days, the White House has shelved plans for Trump to appear on Saturday in Kansas, the site of an unexpectedly competitive Senate campaign, a Republican campaign official said.

“I don’t feel like I have to go to Kansas,” Trump told reporters.

Instead, the president will participate in more than 20 virtual campaign appearances before Tuesday, a White House official said.

“These events give him the opportunity to highlight his accomplishments and expand his reach across the country,” the official said.

The Times reported on Wednesday that Peltola aides worked with campaign lawyers and staff at the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee to recruit two candidates who could siphon votes from the incumbent Republican Sullivan, including a retired teacher named Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., who is on the ballot without a party affiliation.

Peltola’s former campaign manager, Elisa Rios, who was fired in August, told the Times that Peltola was aware of the effort.

Peltola’s campaign said it “has no involvement with either Sullivan campaign.” The DSCC also denied involvement and accused Republicans of propping up candidates of their own in other races.

Jessica Levinson, a professor who specializes in election law at Loyola Law School in Los Angeles, said that as long as Daniel J. Sullivan, the challenger to the incumbent, didn’t conceal financial support, his campaign likely didn’t break any laws and political parties are allowed to mislead the public.

Policing such behavior would open the door to the government investigating why candidates choose to run and why voters support them, she said. “To the extent that people are uncomfortable with two Sullivans, I would offer you’re probably going to be uncomfortable with a really high level of government intrusion into our elections as well.”

TRUMP IN SOUTH CAROLINA, HARRIS IN GEORGIA

Trump held a rally in Rock Hill, South Carolina, on Thursday, his second visit in two weeks to a state where opinion polls show an unexpectedly close Senate race between Republican Darline Graham and Democrat Annie Andrews.

Speaking about the hotly contested Michigan Senate race, where progressive Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed holds a small lead in most polls over Republican Mike Rogers, Trump continued his identity-based attacks on El-Sayed, a Muslim, by saying at the rally that “if you’re Black or if you’re Jewish, and if you vote for Abdul, you’re crazy.”

With control of the Senate at stake, both parties are deploying their biggest names in the closing days of the campaign, with Trump stumping for Republicans and former President Barack Obama and former Vice President Kamala Harris campaigning for Democrats in competitive races.

Harris stumped in Macon, Georgia, at a get-out-the-vote effort. Democrats are aiming to see Senator Jon Ossoff, who leads in polling, reelected, and hope that Keisha Lance Bottoms, locked in a tight race, can become the first woman elected as governor in the state.

Trump’s approval rating stood at 32% in a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday, near a record low, as Americans sour on the high cost of living and the war with Iran.

Some 43.6 million Americans had already voted as of Thursday morning, according to the University of Florida’s Election Lab. A total of 45.9 million voted early in the 2022 midterms.

(Reporting by Jacob Bogage in Rock Hill, South Carolina, Luc Cohen in New York and Bo Erickson in Washington, additional reporting by Andrew Goudsward, Richard Cowan, Nolan D. McCaskill, Ryan Patrick Jones, Tom Hals, Katharine Jackson; Writing by Brad Brooks and Costas Pitas; editing by Scott Malone and Howard Goller)

Four killed in crash of Italian helicopter on EU mission in Bosnia

Reuters

30 October, 2026 03:00 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

ROME/ATHENS, Oct 29 (Reuters) – An Italian military helicopter operating with the EU peacekeeping mission in Bosnia and Herzegovina crashed on Thursday, killing four people and injuring 11 others, Italy’s defence ministry said.

Two of those killed were members of the Italian army and two belonged to the Italian Red Cross’s Volunteer Military Corps, the ministry said. It added that all 11 injured were receiving treatment and none was in a life-threatening condition. A total of 15 people were on board.

“At this moment of immense grief, my thoughts go first and foremost to the families of our fallen, to whom I extend my personal condolences and those of the entire Defence establishment,” Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto said.

Show Full Article

ANSA news agency reported the helicopter came down in the village of Gorice in Brcko district. Images carried by local media showed a military transport helicopter overturned on the ground and shattered into pieces.

“There are no words capable of easing such a profound loss,” Crosetto said.

The aircraft had been deployed as part of Operation Althea, run by the European Union Force, which oversees the implementation of the Dayton Peace Agreement.

Italy’s defence ministry said the cause of the crash was under investigation and that inquiries were underway to establish the circumstances of the accident.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni also expressed her condolences, writing on X: “My thoughts are with the victims, their families, and all those who, as part of the mission to promote peace and stability in the region are experiencing hours of anguish.”

(Reporting by Francesca Piscioneri and Angelo Amante; Additional reporting by Aleksandar Vasovic; Editing by Alvise Armellini, Andrew Heavens and Jamie Freed)

item.title: ＮＹ外為市場＝ユーロ上昇、ＥＣＢ据え置きも12月利上げに含み
item.description: ［ニューヨーク／ロンドン ２９日 ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場では、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が金利据え置きを決定し...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ外為市場＝ユーロ上昇、ＥＣＢ据え置きも12月利上げに含み 6:07 配信

米ドル、ユーロ、円、英ポンドなどの紙幣。3月24日撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic（ロイター） ［ニューヨーク／ロンドン　２９日　ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場では、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が金利据え置きを決定したものの１２月の利上げに含みを残したことを受け、ユーロが上昇した。ドルは経済指標でインフレ加速が示されたことでおおむね軟調。円は日銀が３１日に発表する金融政策決定会合の結果が注目される中、対ドルでほぼ横ばいで推移した。

ＥＣＢはこの日に開いた理事会で、予想通りに金利据え置きを決定。ただ、エネルギー価格の急騰を受けてインフレリスクが高まっていると警告し、１２月の利上げの可能性に含みを残した。ＥＣＢはまた、ラガルド総裁が来年２月７日に退任すると発表。任期は２７年１０月までだった。

ソルトマーシュ・エコノミクスの欧州担当エコノミスト、マルシェル・アレクサンドロビッチ氏は「ＥＣＢは予想通りに金利を据え置いたが、インフレ見通しの上振れリスクを挙げ、１２月の利上げが十分にあり得ることを示唆した」と指摘。「金利据え置きよりも、ラガルド総裁が来年１０月ではなく２月に退任すると発表されたことが大きなニュースだった」とし、１月初めに退任するイザベル・シュナーベル専務理事と、５月に退任予定のフィリップ・レーン専務理事兼チーフエコノミストに言及し、「（ラガルド氏の早期退任は）市場にとって驚きではなかったが、ＥＣＢが２０２７年前半に大規模な人事刷新を迎えることが改めて意識される」と述べた。

ユーロは対ドルで一時５月以来の安値を付けたものの、その後は上向き、終盤の取引で０．１３％高の１．１１６７ドル。

日銀は２９─３０日の金融政策決定会合で金利据え置きを決定すると広く予想されている。バンク・オブ・アメリカのイズミ・デバリエ氏らアナリストは投資家向けリポートで「日銀の政策決定会合で円相場が大きく動くとは予想していないが、基調的なインフレ圧力が根強いことを踏まえると、タカ派的な反対票が複数出れば円高方向の反応が強まる可能性がある」とした。

終盤の取引で円は対ドル で０．０５％安の１５７．９１円。

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）は２８日までの２日間の日程で開いた連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で金利据え置きを決定。１１月３日に中間選挙を控える中、インフレ動向に関する一段のデータを見極める姿勢を示した。ただ、商務省がこの日に発表した９月の個人消費支出（ＰＣＥ）価格指数は前年比３．６％上昇し、伸びは８月の３．４％から加速。ＦＲＢが１２月の次回会合で追加利上げに動くとの見方が強まった。

ＣＭＥフェドウォッチによると、ＦＲＢが１２月の会合で利上げを決定する確率は約８０％。

主要通貨に対するドル指数は０．１４％安の１０１．９８。

item.title: 米スタバ、通期利益見通しが市場予想上回る 10億ドル自社株買い
item.description:
Neil J Kanatt Waylon Cunningham
[２９日 ロイター] - 米コーヒーチェーン大手スター...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米スタバ、通期利益見通しが市場予想上回る 10億ドル自社株買い 6:03 配信

2020年3月6日、英国ロンドンのスターバックス店内　REUTERS/Henry Nicholls（ロイター） Neil J Kanatt　Waylon Cunningham

[２９日　ロイター] - 米コーヒーチェーン大手スターバックスが２９日発表した２０２７年度通期業績見通しで、調整後の１株利益が市場予想を上回った。１０億ドルの自社株買い計画も発表した。ブライアン・ニコル最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）が進める大規模な事業再建に伴うコスト削減や業務改革が効果を上げ始めていることが示された。

ただ、中国事業の売却に伴い通期の減収を予想したことを受け、株価は時間外取引で約２％下落した。

ニコル氏は決算説明会で、同社の「バック・トゥ・スターバックス」戦略はもはや再建策ではなく、成長計画だと投資家に繰り返し説明した。過去２年間、待ち時間の短縮とサービス向上に向け、メニューの簡素化や人員への投資、業務改善を進めてきた。

スターバックスは、通期の調整後１株利益（ＥＰＳ）が３．１５─３．２５ドルになると予想。ＬＳＥＧがまとめたアナリスト予想平均の３．１４ドルを上回った。

ニコル氏は、今後１年はテクノロジーの活用と近代化に重点を置くと説明。ドライブスルーでの注文受け付けを支援する人工知能（ＡＩ）システムのほか、「対象の顧客が来店した際に認識し、個人に合わせたデジタルメニューを提示して、支払いをよりスムーズにする」システムを例に挙げた。

また、サプライチェーン（供給網）の改革も進展していると述べた。商品の需要を予測する新たな手法を試験導入しており、北米では毎日配送を受ける店舗の割合が９０％近くに達しているという。

２６年度第４・四半期（７─９月）の既存店売上高は世界全体で前年同期比７．２％増。市場予想の５．４％増を上回った。調整後１株利益は０．８０ドルとなり、市場予想の０．７２ドルを上回った。

コンシューマー・エッジのアナリスト、マイケル・ガンサー氏は、売上高の伸びは心強く、手頃な価格で楽しめるぜいたくへの需要を反映していると指摘。ただ、スターバックスの若年層の顧客は、急成長する「７ブリュー」などの競合に流出し続けていると警告した。

スターバックスは２７年度の売上高について、市場予想の１．４％増に対し、約１％減を見込んだ。中国の店舗運営事業の価値を４０億ドルと評価する取引で、同事業の支配持ち分を売却し、同事業を博裕投資（ボーユー・キャピタル）との新設合弁会社に移管したことを反映した。

アネックス・ウェルス・マネジメントのアナリスト、ブライアン・ジェイコブセン氏は「業績見通しは弱かったが、期待値を低めに設定しようとしているのかもしれない」と述べ、同社には勢いがあるとの見方を示した。

スターバックスは、海外最大の直営店市場である日本事業について、過半数持ち分の売却を検討している。事業価値は約３０億ドルと評価される可能性がある。一方、チポトレ・メキシカン・グリルの買収の可能性が報じられたことを受け、買収観測を否定していた。

ロイター 関連リンク アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず コラム：進む米中デカップリング、中国「保有米国債」の脅威減退か コラム：トランプ米大統領、任期中の利下げは望み薄　市場は高金利長期化を想定 焦点：トランプ政権の影で歩み寄るカナダとＥＵ、準加盟提示でも見える限界 10/30(金) 8:34 最終更新 ロイター

item.description: NEW YORK, Oct 29 : Wall Street's worries about the cost of the AI boom escalated after the market close on Thursday, as results from Amazon and Intel showed the infrastructure race is not only straining the tech industry but affecting consumers.Surging data-center spending, as highlighted in Amazon's massive

Amazon burns cash, Intel flags weak PC demand as AI boom's costs ripple across markets

The logo of Amazon is pictured at a company logistics center in Carquefou near Nantes, westren France, May 6, 2026. REUTERS/Stephane Mahe

FILE PHOTO: An Intel logo and a computer motherboard appear in this illustration taken August 25, 2025. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo

30 Oct 2026 05:02AM (Updated: 30 Oct 2026 09:28AM)

FAST

NEW YORK, Oct 29 : Wall Street's worries about the cost of the AI boom escalated after the market close on Thursday, as results from Amazon and Intel showed the infrastructure race is not only straining the tech industry but affecting consumers. Surging data-center spending, as highlighted in Amazon's massive cash burn, has turned once debt-light tech giants into major borrowers, while price hikes are squeezing global demand for devices like smartphones and PCs. Amazon forecast holiday-quarter sales below Wall Street expectations, a potential sign of growing pressure on consumers as inflation picks up, which also hit Intel's PC business, as a memory chip shortage has driven up its costs. The AI spending spree is also eating into Big Tech's once-enviable cash flows. Alphabet and Meta both burned cash in the September quarter, while Microsoft, the only exception, joined their borrowing binge with a $25 billion debt sale on Thursday.

The tech giants have deep pockets to sustain their spending, but investors have grown increasingly wary of smaller AI cloud firms borrowing heavily to deliver on enormous order backlogs. Amazon's 7 per cent after-hours slide was accompanied by losses of 5.8 per cent to 6.7 per cent in AI cloud stocks CoreWeave, Nebius and Iren. Alphabet, which closed regular trading down nearly 13 per cent, fell another 1.5 per cent after-hours. The semiconductor index also sold off post-close after Intel blamed "near term headwinds across the PC industry." The index had already dropped 1.4 per cent during the regular session due to Alphabet's messy earnings report.  Shares of PC makers HP and Dell sank 8 per cent and 6.8 per cent. "The revenues missed due to lower PC demand and forward guidance also disappointed. As Google learned today, earnings matter," said Kim Caughey Forrest, founder and chief investment officer at Bokeh Capital Partners LLC. Google parent Alphabet dropped 13 per cent on Thursday. INTEL FACTORY SHUTDOWN Intel, whose shares were down 18 per cent, also said a factory explosion in Israel caused a two-week shutdown and would cost it roughly $600 million in lost revenue over two quarters.  "Overall semiconductor weakness after hours is primarily a function of Intel guide and negative sentiment spillover," said Michael James, equity sales trader at Rosenblatt Securities.  Some analysts said Intel's problems in the PC sector, an area of technology that does not garner the same scrutiny on Wall Street as the AI buildout, do not seem to necessarily mean big problems for other chipmakers that operate more prominently in AI. Nevertheless, investors in the less-active post-market trade chose to shoot first and ask questions later. AMD dropped 4 per cent and Broadcom fell 2 per cent. Among the biggest losers in the volatile session was the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull ETF, which offers investors three times the daily performance of the SOX and was off 9 per cent. The SOX has been one of 2026's standout performers, rising more than 60 per cent as shortages of chips and equipment needed for the AI buildout drive up prices and profits at firms ranging from giant Nvidia and memory chip firm Micron to Marvell Technology.  But the momentum of that trade has been tested over the past month by tightening financing terms. That has kept some expected IPOs on the sidelines and put some highly leveraged AI infrastructure firms under pressure. The SOX has declined 13 per cent since hitting its recent high in October and is off 21 per cent from its all-time high in June.  "I think Intel was seen as this unicorn within the tech sector because it was seen as being weaker compared to Nvidia and AMD," said Jake Dollarhide, chief executive officer of Longbow Asset Management in Tulsa, Oklahoma.     "It just had this miraculous rise, and you got a lot of retail money into it, and some of that money is easy come, easy go."

Source: Reuters

Bank of Japan to hold rates, signal further hikes

FAST

TOKYO, Oct 30 : The Bank of Japan is set to keep interest rates steady on Friday but stress its focus on preventing underlying inflation from overshooting its 2 per cent target, suggesting scope to hike borrowing costs as soon as December. Such guidance would reinforce the central bank's message last month that it has entered a new, more hawkish policy phase and is open to raising rates once every few months, analysts said. The pivot would also align the BOJ with its US and European counterparts eyeing near-term rate hikes to battle inflationary risks from the AI boom and the Iran war-induced energy shock. "Global price pressures from AI investment are quite strong, which means the recent inflation is partly demand driven," said Kazuo Momma, a former BOJ executive who is currently executive economist at Mizuho Research Institute.

"By declaring that its policy phase has changed, the BOJ is essentially telling markets it will hike rates once a quarter," he said, predicting rate hikes in December and March next year. At the two-day meeting ending on Friday, the BOJ is set to maintain its policy rate at 1.25 per cent, forgoing a back-to-back hike to spend more time scrutinising the effect of past rate hikes on lending conditions. In a quarterly report, the BOJ is likely to slightly revise up next fiscal year's price forecast and signal that underlying inflation has roughly achieved its 2 per cent target, people familiar with the matter have told Reuters. With wage gains becoming embedded and inflation expectations hovering around 2 per cent, the central bank will likely stress that it will now focus on anchoring inflation around its target by raising rates toward levels deemed neutral to the economy. Markets will scrutinise comments from Governor Kazuo Ueda's post-meeting news conference for hints on the pace and timing of further rate hikes. "If the BOJ were to say underlying inflation reached levels consistent with its 2 per cent price target, that would have important policy implications," said former BOJ official Nobuyasu Atago, who is currently chief economist at Rakuten Securities Economic Research Institute. "It would be a show of resolve the BOJ won't tolerate any further overshoot in inflation," and signal the chance of more nimble rate hikes next year, he said. With stubbornly high energy costs and rising import prices from a weak yen adding to inflationary pressures, the BOJ raised rates in September after delivering a hike in June - a shorter interval than the roughly twice-a-year hikes in 2024 and 2025. Most analysts polled by Reuters expect the BOJ to raise its policy rate to 1.5 per cent in December, followed by further hikes next year. Their terminal rate projection centres around 1.75 per cent to 2 per cent. Annual core inflation in Tokyo, seen as a leading indicator of nationwide price trends, well exceeded the central bank's 2 per cent target in October, data showed on Friday, highlighting mounting price pressure. Rising prices could weigh on consumption as they prod Japanese households, many of whom have never experienced widespread price gains in their lifetime, to seek discounts. In current quarterly projections made in July, the BOJ expects consumer inflation to accelerate in coming months as firms continue to pass on rising costs.

Source: Reuters

Exclusive-Greek PM calls Turkey-Libya maritime deal ‘void;’ calls for global truce after Black Sea attacks

Reuters

30 October, 2026 02:30 am IST

Facebook

Follow Us :

By Antoni Slodkowski UNITED NATIONS, Oct 29 (Reuters) – Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said on Thursday that the recently signed maritime deal between Libya’s eastern parliament and Turkey was “blatantly illegal, null and void,” adding that it “completely disregards the geography.”

Mitsotakis, speaking to Reuters as Greece ends its UN Security Council presidency, also called for an urgent “international truce” to protect shipping in the Black Sea after the sinking of a Greek-owned container vessel on Wednesday.

Libya’s eastern parliament last week approved a maritime boundaries deal with Turkey, drawing condemnation from Athens, but also Egypt, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates, as a threat to regional security and international legal order.

Show Full Article

“It completely disregards the geography, the reality that there are Greek islands — they seem to completely disappear in the thinking of Turkey and Libya,” Mitsotakis said, accusing them of attempting to create a “fait accompli” that ignores the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.

Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan has said that reactions from the EU and others to the approval of the agreement, originally agreed in 2019, had no legitimate basis, defending Ankara’s policy in the eastern Mediterranean.

Since the 2019 Libya-Turkey deal, Greece has awarded a license to a consortium led by Chevron to look for gas off the island of Crete and has sought a separate agreement with Libya on demarcating their maritime zones.

Mitsotakis assured “there’s no risk that these explorations will be in any way challenged.”

Referring to Libya and Greece as “natural neighbors,” Mitsotakis, who first became prime minister in 2019 and is in his second term, urged the African country to negotiate directly with Athens and take the discussions “very, very seriously.”

ATTACKS ON SHIPS IN THE BLACK SEA

Mitsotakis, 58, spoke to Reuters after chairing a council debate on maritime security, only hours after a Greek container ship sank after being hit by naval drones off Bulgaria in the latest strike on ships in the western Black Sea this month.

Greek-operated ships are among the world’s largest fleets of tankers and are pivotal for trade across the Black Sea region, whose waters are shared by Bulgaria, Georgia, Romania and Turkey, as well as warring Russia and Ukraine, which Moscow invaded in February 2022.

“We do need some sort of international truce when it comes to the freedom of navigation,” said Mitsotakis, adding that it was of “utmost priority” to allow for exports of grain from the region into the world through the Black Sea.

“Greek shipowners would be the first to resume trading in the Black Sea, also from Ukraine, assuming a safe passage is guaranteed,” he said, stressing the rising costs of shipping as chartering and insurance expenses have “gone through the roof.”

It was not immediately clear who had carried out the attack, which added to growing concerns about the impact of Russia’s war in Ukraine on commercial shipping in the area.

Mitsotakis said that Ukraine was financially dependent on exports of its products: “They had a bumper harvest, but the grain is now sitting in silos, in danger of rotting.”

“Unfortunately, for the moment, Russia doesn’t seem to be interested in engaging in a substantive discussion,” he said.

RED SEA SECURITY, RUSSIA

Mitsotakis also called on the European Union to bolster its naval mission to protect shipping in the Red Sea called Aspides, which was launched in 2024 to protect from attacks by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis.

Intensifying hostilities between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia have disrupted oil supplies and heightened the risk of a wider regional conflict, eight months since the US-Israeli strikes on Iran.

“My argument is simple: the European Union has an interest in having a concrete presence with hard assets in this part of the world, and we need more countries to participate in Aspides,” Mitsotakis told Reuters.

He said Greece, Italy and France have deployed “assets” as part of the mission and that was “clearly not enough.” Diplomats told Reuters as of late September there were six warships operating as part of the operation.

The Houthis said this week they had attacked Saudi military aircraft and repelled an advance by Saudi-backed forces near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, an important Red Sea shipping route.

“If we really want to send the message also to the Gulf countries that we take their security seriously, but we also protect the critical arteries and waterways that are absolutely indispensable for European trade, we should be willing to deploy more assets to this part of the world,” Mitsotakis said.

Asked about US President Donald Trump’s move earlier this month to lift sanctions on Russian diesel exports, Mitsotakis reaffirmed Greek support for sanctions on Moscow.

“We believe that we need to put economic pressure and impose more financial pain on Russia to send a very clear signal that as long as they prolong this war, they will suffer very specific economic consequences,” he said.

(Reporting by Antoni Slodkowski; Editing by Andrea Ricci)

Venezuela to offer state assets to private sector, Rodriguez says

Oct 29 (Reuters) – Venezuela’s interim President Delcy Rodriguez said on Thursday the government has made progress identifying state assets to offer to the private sector and former owners, a move that could reverse nationalizations ordered by former President Hugo Chavez.

“I have instructed that non-essential assets held by the state be assessed to determine which can be offered to the private sector or returned to their former owners. This process is already well advanced,” Rodriguez said in a televised address.

In April, Rodriguez appointed a government commission to audit and evaluate state-owned assets, including infrastructure in industries such as energy, power and mining. They have been working on asset classification since, according to people familiar with the matter.

Show Full Article

She did not provide further details on the process. Under Chavez, the nationalization of key projects and industries left over a dozen international arbitration claims, which mostly remain unsettled by the government.

In her speech, Rodriguez said 44 energy contracts are being negotiated under the state’s oil law approved in January. The government has stated that 61 oil agreements have been signed, without providing details.

“Similarly, important negotiations are under way in the mining sector, specifically regarding gold, aluminum, and iron,” she added.

The president also said she has instructed law enforcement agencies not to arrest people without a warrant, and vowed to defend the right to “peaceful protest” in the country, which has a history of political repression and last week experienced its first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years.

“The responsible exercise of political rights is guaranteed for everyone. Our doors are open,” Rodriguez said.

In her address, Rodriguez said the government has planned four quarterly increases in the national minimum wage in 2027.

During a separate afternoon appearance on state television, Rodriguez said diplomat Oliver Blanco, previously the vice foreign minister, will take over as the country’s top diplomat.

His predecessor, Felix Plasencia, will become presidential adviser for international affairs, Rodriguez said.

(Reporting by Anthony Esposito;Editing by Rod Nickel)

item.title: エヌビディアＣＥＯ、シンガポール企業との取引擁護 元幹部に中国スパイ疑惑＝報道
item.description: [２９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[２９日 ロイター] - 米半導体大手のエヌビディアのジェンスン・フアン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は、シンガポールに拠点を置くメガスピード・インターナショナルとの取引を擁護し、「通常のことであり、異例ではない」と述べた。ブルームバーグ・ニュースが２９日報じた。

これに先立ち、ニューヨーク・タイムズ（ＮＹＴ）は、メガスピードの元幹部の１人が中国のためにスパイ活動をした疑いで米当局の捜査を受けていると報じていた。

ブルームバーグ・ニュースによると、フアン氏は、メガスピード幹部との関係は適切なものであり、メガスピードがエヌビディアの人工知能（ＡＩ）チップを中国に不正に出荷していないことを確認していたと説明。「われわれは当社の画像処理装置（ＧＰＵ）の配備状況を全て調べ、一つ残らず確認した」と述べた。

ＮＹＴの報道によると、フアン氏は、この元幹部とのやり取りは中国の顧客や経営幹部との典型的なものであり、この人物はすでにメガスピードを退社していると語った。同報道によると、エヌビディアは、米国の輸出規制があるにもかかわらず、同社の先端ＡＩチップの中国への密輸は重大な問題ではないと主張しているという。

item.title: 米アマゾン、クラウド好調もＡＩ投資で現金流出加速 株価7％安
item.description:
Deborah Mary Sophia Greg Bensinger
[２９日 ロイター] - 米アマゾン・ドット・コ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米アマゾン、クラウド好調もＡＩ投資で現金流出加速　株価7％安 5:25 配信

２０２５年１１月撮影　 REUTERS/Stephanie Lecocq（ロイター） Deborah Mary Sophia　Greg Bensinger

[２９日 ロイター] - 米アマゾン・ドット・コムが２９日発表した第３・四半期決算は、クラウド事業の成長加速が続いた一方、人工知能（ＡＩ）需要の取り込みに向けた積極投資を背景に現金流出が膨らんだ。２０２７年の設備投資が２６年からさらに増加するとの見通しも示し、株価が急落した。

第４・四半期（１０─１２月）の売上高は２４００億─２４７０億ドルと予想。レンジの中央値（２４３５億ドル）はＬＳＥＧがまとめた市場予想の２４４５億１０００万ドルをやや下回った。

株価は時間外取引で一時７％下落。通常取引でも４．３％下落していた。

第３・四半期は直近１２カ月ベースの現金流出が４２４億ドルとなった。設備投資が７７２億６０００万ドルと、ＬＳＥＧがまとめた市場予想を約２００億ドル上回った。

前期は７６億ドルの現金流出、前年同期は１４８億ドルの現金創出を報告していた。

アプタス・キャピタル・アドバイザーズのポートフォリオマネジャー、デーブ・ワグナー氏は「今回の決算で悪い部分はフリーキャッシュフローのようだ。事業活動で潤沢な現金を生み出したが、設備投資がそれを完全に飲み込んでしまった」と指摘。「このトレンドはかなり急で、かなりマイナスだ。それが今回の決算で懸念される大きな点だ」と語った。

アマゾンは競合他社と同様、ＡＩソフトウエアとインフラの開発に巨額を投じる方針で、２６年の設備投資を２２００億ドルと見込んでいる。同社は今回、この見通しを据え置いた。

アンディ・ジャシー最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）はアナリスト向け電話会議で、２７年の設備投資は２６年を「大幅に上回る」との見通しを示したが、詳細は明らかにしなかった。

「われわれの戦略は機能しており、当面はそれが続くと見込んでいる」と述べ、投資家の懸念払拭に努めた。クラウドコンピューティング部門「アマゾン・ウェブ・サービス（ＡＷＳ）」の売上高は早ければ５年で１兆ドルに達する可能性があるとし、「ＡＷＳの機能とインフラへの投資は成果を上げている」と述べた。また「アマゾンの売上規模に迫る他の小売企業は見当たらない」と語った。

ただ、インベスティング・ドット・コムのシニアアナリスト、ジェシー・コーエン氏は、株価下落の理由としてフリーキャッシュフローと「弱い業績見通し」を挙げ、「アマゾンの第３・四半期決算は二重の失望を招いた」と述べた。

＜クラウド事業が成長けん引＞

第３・四半期のＡＷＳの売上高は前年比３９％増の４６０億ドル。伸び率は第２・四半期の３７％からやや加速し、約５年ぶりの高水準となった。ＬＳＥＧがまとめた市場予想は３８．２％増の４５６億１０００万ドルだった。

広告事業の売上高は失望を誘う内容で、前年比１２％増の１９６億ドルにとどまり、ＬＳＥＧがまとめた予想（１８％増）を下回った。広告売上高がアナリスト予想を下回るのは７四半期ぶり。伸び率は第２・四半期の２６％、２５年第３・四半期の２２％から大幅に鈍化した。

それでもジャシー氏は広告売上高に「満足している」と述べ、割引セール「プライムデー」の開催時期を第２・四半期に移したことが、第３・四半期の広告売上高全体に影響したと説明した。第４・四半期には「１０％台後半」の伸びに戻ると予想した。

ロイター 関連リンク アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず コラム：ＩＴサービス企業、生成ＡＩ追い風に株価上昇か コラム：ＡＩ投資を「黄金」に変えたマイクロソフト、アルファベットは羨望か コラム：米アップル、ＥＶ断念でもＡＩによる収益化期待揺るがず 10/30(金) 9:26 最終更新 ロイター

item.title: 米国株式市場＝反落、アルファベット決算受けＡＩ投資に警戒
item.description: ［ニューヨーク ２９日 ロイター］ - 米国株式市場は反落した。注目企業の決算や重要なインフレ指標を消化する中で、投資家...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米国株式市場＝反落、アルファベット決算受けＡＩ投資に警戒 5:25 配信

2026年10月28日、米のニューヨーク証券取引所（NYSE）REUTERS/Jeenah Moon（ロイター） ［ニューヨーク　２９日　ロイター］ - 米国株式市場は反落した。注目企業の決算や重要なインフレ指標を消化する中で、投資家は大手テクノロジー企業による巨額のＡＩ（人工知能）投資を見直した。

主要３株価指数はいずれも下落。２８日に発表されたアルファベットの低調な四半期決算を受け、テクノロジー株比率の高いナスダックの下げが最も大きかった。一方、小型株で構成するラッセル２０００指数は１．０％上昇した。

半導体株は５営業日ぶりに反落。野心的なＡＩ投資の資金を自力で賄える企業と、手元資金を取り崩し借り入れに頼る企業を選別する動きが広がった。

アルファベットは前日の決算発表を受けて後者と見なされた。中核の検索広告事業が振るわず売上高が市場予想を下回ったほか、ＡＩ関連の資金流出も大幅に拡大した。株価は１２．６％急落し、通信サービス指数を押し下げた。

ベアードの投資戦略アナリスト、ロス・メイフィールド氏は「こうしたリスク回避の日に小型株が相対的に好調なのは、ＡＩの成長シナリオにほころびが見えても市場全体に問題が広がるわけではないと、市場が今のところ受け止めていることを示す良い兆候だ」と指摘。「ＡＩ関連株以外にも、かなり有望な投資先は数多くある」と述べた。

米商務省が発表した第３・四半期の国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）速報値は前期比年率３．４％増加し、市場予想を上回った。底堅い個人消費とＡＩ関連の企業投資が、中東紛争に伴う原油価格上昇の影響を補い、成長率は１年ぶりの高い伸びとなった。また、９月の個人消費支出（ＰＣＥ）価格指数は前年比３．６％上昇し、８月の３．４％上昇から伸びが加速した。

重機大手キャタピラーは９．３％下落。四半期利益が市場予想を上回ったものの、成長目標を据え置いた。

一方、第３・四半期売上高が市場予想を上回ったフォード・モーターは１２．４％上昇した。

製薬大手イーライ・リリーは６．６％高。肥満症治療薬の好調な販売を受け、売上高見通しを引き上げた。

メルクも３．８％上昇。がん治療薬「キイトルーダ」とヒトパピローマウイルス（ＨＰＶ）ワクチン「ガーダシル」の販売が好調で、利益が市場予想を上回った。

ソフトウエア株は総じて軟調で、フォーティネットとサービスナウは四半期決算発表後にいずれも２０％超下落した。

半導体大手マーベル・テクノロジーは１３．２％下落。データセンター向け光学部品を手がけるルメンタム・ホールディングスの買収に向け、詰めの協議を進めていると報じられた。ルメンタムは０．６％上昇した。

アマゾン・ドット・コムは第４・四半期の売上高見通しが失望を誘い、時間外取引で６．５％下落した。

ニューヨーク証券取引所では値上がり銘柄数が値下がり銘柄数を１．９５対１の比率で上回った。ナスダックでも１．０７対１で値上がり銘柄が多かった。

米取引所の合算出来高は約１７０億５０００万株。直近２０営業日の平均は１７０億９０００万株。

Coinbase returns to profit as crypto investment gains offset trading weakness

FAST

Oct 29 : Cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase Global returned to profitability on Thursday after three consecutive quarters of losses, helped by lower operating expenses and investment gains on crypto assets that cushioned weaker trading activity. The results underscore the company's continued exposure to swings in crypto asset prices, with gains in the value of its investment portfolio helping boost earnings even as challenging market conditions weighed on trading volumes and transaction revenue, its largest source of income. Transaction revenue dropped 43 per cent to $590.2 million in the third quarter, from $1.05 billion a year earlier. Shares of the crypto exchange were down 3.3 per cent in trading after the bell. The company said macro headwinds have begun to shift and crypto prices rebounded in September.

REVENUE DIVERSIFICATION GAINS TRACTION Prediction markets emerged as another area of growth for Coinbase during the reported quarter, with revenue exceeding $200 million. Chief Financial Officer Alesia Haas said prediction markets and derivatives together accounted for about 25 per cent of its total transaction revenue, while subscription and services revenue made up roughly 49 per cent of total net revenue. "We are seeing the investments that we've made over the past few years to really diversify our revenue, really come to our benefit," Haas said. Coinbase's prediction markets had become one of the fastest-growing products in the company's history, helping drive additional spot trading volume, Third Bridge analyst Jacob Zuller said. The expansion also reflects its strategy of diversifying revenue streams beyond its core transaction business, which remains heavily dependent on crypto-market activity. "They (Coinbase) also treat the category (prediction markets) as near-term revenue, with derivatives as the longer bet," said Colby Howard, president of Heron Events at Heron Intelligence. "They also see prediction markets as a way in, with traders who start making money moving up to the paid tier," Howard said. Total operating expenses in the third quarter fell about 17 per cent to $1.15 billion, compared with $1.39 billion in the prior year. The Wilmington, Delaware-based firm reported a profit of $718.7 million, or $2.51 per share, for the quarter ended September 30, compared with $432.6 million, or $1.50 per share, a year earlier.

Source: Reuters

Oct 29 : Walmart said on Thursday it had extended its agreement with AI robotics firm Symbotic, committing about $6 billion over several years to bring more automation capabilities to its distribution network. Symbotic has been helping Walmart automate its supply chain since 2017. Under the agreement, Symbotic will bring additional automation capabilities to 25 of Walmart's regional distribution centers in the US and support its supply chain capabilities globally. Walmart said the agreement aimed to support its e-commerce upstream inventory management, increase storage capacity and improve how products move through the supply chain. These capabilities will help Walmart offer customers a broader assortment, improve speed and provide more reliable replenishment across its network, the retailer said. Retailers are increasingly deploying chatbots, along with targeted promotions and loyalty programs to entice shoppers who often turn to AI for product recommendations.

FAST

Oct 29 : Reddit CEO Steve Huffman outlined a plan on Thursday to mandate sign-ins for most content to deter data scraping on the social media platform after he blamed Google's AI search features for a decline in referral traffic. Shares of Reddit fell 18 per cent in extended trading after Huffman warned that total daily active unique visitors could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter from about 130 million if referral traffic continues to fall. Search engine referrals to Reddit decreased by more than one million on average each week during October, he said. In the US, DAUq fell 2 per cent to 50.7 million, marking its first decline since Reddit went public in 2024. "Google is crawling us as hard as ever, so the demand hasn't changed from their point of view either. The reality is, the AI mode does not drive traffic, not for us and not to anybody," Huffman added on a post earnings call.

AI-powered search is answering user queries directly, cutting off traffic to publishers and social media firms and threatening the user growth essential to their advertising business. "Requiring users to log in creates another barrier to engagement, particularly for casual users," said Luke Stillman, a managing director at research firm Madison and Wall. Reddit, which licenses its data to OpenAI and Google, has sued IPO-bound Anthropic, Perplexity AI and three data scraping companies, accusing them of illegally collecting Reddit's data. The company's trove of user-generated discussions is a prized asset, offering AI startups data to train models and helping marketers get insights for ads. "We will continue licensing our corpus intentionally, but those commercial deals come with guardrails that protect our users and our business," Huffman said in a statement. Reddit's 53 per cent revenue growth slowed sequentially in the third quarter, but is still better than firms including Snap and Pinterest, as they compete for ad dollars with bigger rival Meta in a tough market. CFO Drew Vollero said Reddit crossed $3 billion in trailing 12-month revenue in the third quarter and the company's next "internal north star is $5 billion in revenue. Reddit plans to test the logged-in-only experience in select markets outside of US in the fourth quarter to assess its impact before wider implementation, the shift that would end two decades of allowing anyone to browse Reddit freely without an account. Huffman said logged-in users make up over 80 per cent of the monetization. The firm's third-quarter revenue of $895 million exceeded LSEG-compiled analysts' average estimate of $878.4 million. Its revenue forecast for the current quarter of $1.00 billion to $1.03 billion is largely in line with estimates. It expects quarterly adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization to be between $480 million and $510 million, versus estimates of $512.2 million.

Source: Reuters

FAST

Oct 29 : Amazon.com on Thursday reported a massive cash burn in the third quarter, sending shares sharply lower, while it signaled higher capital expenditures next year atop an already huge amount in 2026. Amazon's cloud computing cash cow, Amazon Web Services, continued to accelerate, but the company's aggressive spending to capture AI demand overshadowed broader growth that investors typically crave — with more such spending to come. The Seattle-based retailer expects revenue between $240.0 billion and $247.0 billion in the fourth quarter, bracketing estimates of $244.51 billion, according to LSEG, but its midpoint of $243.5 billion came in slightly lower. Investors soured on the company, driving shares down as much as 7 per cent in extended trading, and the shares had declined 4.3 per cent in regular trading to end at $243.79. The drop mirrored a broader selloff among tech stocks on Thursday after Intel warned of flagging PC revenue through next year's first half, sending its shares down 23 per cent in after-hours trading. Alphabet shares fell 12 per cent during the regular session, their worst single-day percentage decline ever.

The company said it burned $42.4 billion on a trailing 12-month basis in the September quarter, driven by capital expenditure of $77.26 billion, which was some $20 billion above estimates, according to data compiled by LSEG. Amazon reported cash burn of $7.6 billion in the prior quarter, and generated $14.8 billion in the third quarter of last year. "The free cash flow looks like the ugly part of the report," said Dave Wagner, portfolio manager at Aptus Capital Advisors. "Operations generated plenty of cash but their capex just absolutely swallowed it." "The trend is pretty steep and pretty negative, and that's the big thing that is alarming in this report." Like competitors, Amazon has made a huge spending commitment to developing AI software and infrastructure, forecasting $220 billion in capital expenditures this year. Amazon and Google parent Alphabet have maintained their spending expectations, though Microsoft on Wednesday lowered its own to $170 billion from $175 billion. CEO Andy Jassy told analysts on a conference call he expected capital expenditures to be "meaningfully more" next year, compared with 2026, without elaborating. Jassy tried to lessen investor concerns following the results. "Our strategy is working and I expect it will for the foreseeable future," he said. He said AWS could reach a trillion dollars in revenue in as little as five years, adding, "our AWS investment in functionality and infrastructure is working.” He also said, "I'm not aware of another retail business approaching Amazon's revenue size." Still, Jesse Cohen, a senior analyst at Investing.com, also pointed to Amazon's free cash flow and "weak guidance" as reasons for the share decline. "Amazon's third-quarter report landed as a double disappointment." CLOUD BUSINESS DRIVES GROWTH Revenue at Amazon Web Services rose 39 per cent to $46 billion in the third quarter ended September, compared with analysts' estimate for a 38.2 per cent increase to $45.61 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. AWS revenue recorded a 37 per cent jump in the second quarter. Advertising sales were another disappointment, rising just 12 per cent to $19.6 billion from a year earlier, below the 18 per cent estimate from LSEG — the first time they missed analyst estimates in seven quarters. The results marked much slower growth than the second quarter's 26 per cent or the 2025 third quarter's 22 per cent. Jassy, nonetheless, said he was "pleased" with advertising sales and said moving the Prime Day discount event to the second quarter had impacted overall ads in the period. He forecast a return to "high teens" ad sales growth in the current quarter. He dismissed concerns that AI shopping agents, which automate people's purchasing, had impacted ad sales. The company during the quarter blocked Meta's Muse agent from accessing its site to shop on customers' behalf. The downbeat fourth-quarter outlook signals US retailers could face pain in the holiday season, as consumers tighten shopping budgets amid higher gasoline prices and the rising cost of living. Still, recent industry forecasts predict holiday sales will accelerate from last year. The National Retail Federation earlier this month predicted a 4.2 per cent jump in total US holiday season sales. While retail sales account for the majority of Amazon's revenue, investor focus has shifted sharply toward its cloud computing business, Amazon Web Services, in recent years, as the tech company spends heavily to build out data centers and compete in the global AI race. Amazon's cloud unit grew at its fastest pace in nearly five years. At its e-commerce business, Amazon has been rolling out faster delivery services globally and expanding to more rural areas in the US to draw more shoppers.

Source: Reuters

item.description: Oct 29 : Intel shares plunged 23 per cent after hours on Thursday after the chip maker warned it would burn cash this year due to the faltering PC market, bottlenecks in manufacturing and heavy spending on expanding production.Like many other major tech companies, Intel has been pouring money into manufacturi

FAST

Oct 29 : Intel shares plunged 23 per cent after hours on Thursday after the chip maker warned it would burn cash this year due to the faltering PC market, bottlenecks in manufacturing and heavy spending on expanding production. Like many other major tech companies, Intel has been pouring money into manufacturing, but has run into supply disruptions that have capped its ability to capitalize on growing demand for data-center chips. Compounding that pressure, PC costs are on the rise due to the surge in memory prices, which has weighed on demand. That weak demand could persist through the first half of 2027, Intel warned on Thursday, and also forecast December-quarter revenue below market expectations. Intel expects the deadly October explosion at its Israel plant to erase roughly $600 million in revenue over two quarters and reduce supplies of AI server chips to cloud customers, Intel told Reuters in an interview.

"I'm disappointed that we were not able to meet strong customer demand in this quarter," Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on a conference call with analysts. "We face near-term challenges, including manufacturing supply shortages, the unprecedented memory crunch, and the resulting softness in PC demand." The gloomy outlook reverberated across the chip sector. Nvidia, Broadcom, AMD, Micron, Qualcomm and Arm Holdings' US-listed shares fell between 1 per cent and 6 per cent in extended trading. If Intel's stock were to lose 23 per cent in Friday's regular session, it would shed more than $112 billion in market value. Intel's stock has more than doubled this year. "I think we entered earnings season with the market in a pessimistic mood. No result is good enough, and bad results receive extra punishment," said Seaport Research Partners analyst Jay Goldberg. The company expects PC chip revenue to decline in the mid-20 per cent range for its fourth quarter, after a 5 per cent drop to $8.10 billion in the third quarter. Intel expects fourth-quarter revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion, below analysts' average estimate of $17.07 billion, according to LSEG data. Adjusted profit is expected to come in at 25 cents per share, trailing estimates of 43 cents. FACTORY EXPLOSION SQUEEZES CAPACITY The October explosion at Intel's Kiryat Gat, Israel, factory killed two and seriously injured one, according to media reports. Finance chief David Zinsner said Intel planned to ramp up production at the facility by the end of this week after a two-week shutdown. The Kiryat Gat factory largely produces data center chips using the company's 10 nanometer manufacturing process. Intel lowered its fourth-quarter revenue outlook by roughly $300 million and cut its gross margin outlook by about 200 basis points, Zinsner told Reuters. He expects a similar hit in the first quarter. Intel is in the process of determining which wafers are salvageable for use and sale after the blast. "We'll have to see whether there is an impact that stretches beyond that," Zinsner said. "The explosion at Kiryat Gat, one of Intel’s major manufacturing sites, is unfortunate and brought down Intel’s capacity," said Hendi Susanto, portfolio manager at Gabelli Funds. TURNAROUND PLANS Tan has been leading the company's turnaround after it fell behind Nvidia, whose graphics processors dominate the AI boom. Intel's contract manufacturing, or foundry, business is a key part of his strategy. On the conference call with investors, Zinsner said Intel does not expect to have positive cash flow this year as expands manufacturing capacity. He said the company remains on track to spend $20 billion in capital this year and that spending will rise sharply in 2027 as Intel secures more chipmaking tools. Zinsner also said that the costs of 18A, the chipmaking technology used to make the company's "Panther Lake" chips, have fallen 40 per cent since the first quarter, which should help the company's margins longer term. For the third quarter ended September 26, revenue rose 21 per cent to $16.51 billion, in line with estimates. Adjusted profit came in at 52 cents per share, beating estimates of 40 cents.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Iran Receives Vance Letter, Signals No Shift in Peace Deal Terms
item.description: Iran received a letter sent by US Vice President JD Vance to its top security official, the semi-official Tasnim news agency reported, with one of the country’s top negotiators later suggesting Tehran’s positions on ending the war will not be compromised.
item.dc:creator: list.metadata.agency
item.content:encoded: (Bloomberg) -- Iran received a letter sent by US Vice President JD Vance to its top security official, the semi-official Tasnim news agency reported, with one of the country’s top negotiators later suggesting Tehran’s positions on ending the war will not be compromised. Tasnim didn’t disclose the contents of the letter addressed to Mohsen Rezaee, the hardline chief of the Supreme National Security Council, or say whether Tehran is preparing a reply. But in a post on X after the letter was reportedly received, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, one of Iran’s negotiators in previous talks to end the war, wrote that “Iran’s conditions have been repeatedly and clearly stated to the mediators.” “The carrot-and-stick approach has no effect on Iran,” Ghalibaf continued without mentioning Vance’s letter or saying if his comments constituted a formal reply. The highly unusual approach by Vance comes as President Donald Trump repeatedly threatens to resume airstrikes on Iran amid an impasse in negotiations to end the eight-month war. Trump told reporters on Wednesday he authorized Vance to contact Tehran, saying the letter was meant to assist Iran with “medical supplies and various things,” without providing specifics.The Wall Street Journal earlier reported that Vance had written to Rezaee in a bid to revive peace negotiations. The development follows high-level talks in Tehran this week with officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan. The parties described the meeting as positive and agreed to continue discussions, though no formal second round has been set. Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei reiterated earlier this week that his country has certain conditions that must be met before an end to the war can be agreed. At the heart of the impasse is Tehran’s ongoing attacks on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz, while the US has imposed a naval blockade on Iran’s ports. Iran has repeatedly said in recent weeks that it remains open to diplomacy, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi writing on X on Thursday that while “our Brave Armed Forces are fully prepared to defend the Homeland, Iran continues to give diplomacy a chance to succeed.”The US and Israel started bombing Iran in late February, triggering retaliatory strikes by Tehran on Gulf nations hosting US military bases. The war has killed thousands — mostly Iranian civilians — while disrupting energy shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and roiling global markets.--With assistance from Eltaf Najafizada and Sherif Tarek.More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: 米、ベネズエラ大統領選の27年実施を提案＝野党指導者マチャド氏
item.description:
Mayela Armas Deisy Buitrago
[カラカス ２９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Mayela Armas　Deisy Buitrago

[カラカス　２９日　ロイター] - ベネズエラの野党指導者でノーベル平和賞受賞者のマリア・コリナ・マチャド氏は２９日、米国がベネズエラの大統領選を２０２７年に実施するよう提案していると明らかにした。

マチャド氏は２５日に約１年ぶりにベネズエラに帰国。テレビ中継された首都カラカスでの記者会見で「ここ数日の米国務省の声明は、今後取るべき措置について非常に明確だ」と述べ、その内容として新たな国家選挙評議会（ＣＮＥ）の速やかな任命、憲法上の期限の順守、２７年の大統領選実施を挙げた。

また、ルビオ米国務長官は２７年のベネズエラ大統領選実施を支持していると指摘。今後実施されるいかなる選挙でも投票資格を持つ全てのベネズエラ国民が投票できるようにすると述べた。

マチャド氏が本格的な発言を行うのは今回が帰国以来初めて。マチャド氏はこれまでも２７年の大統領選実施を支持してきた。

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州市場サマリー（29日） 4:17 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞

上昇して取引を終えた。石油株が買われて、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は続伸。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．１４％高と反発した。

ＦＴＳＥ３５０種石油・ガス株指数は１．６４％高。石油大手シェルは２．１％上昇。２０２６年７─９月期決算で純利益が２０２２年以来の高水準となったほか、自社株買い計画の拡大を発表したことから買われた。

防衛大手ＢＡＥシステムズは２．２％、エンジンメーカーのロールスロイスは１．３％、それぞれ上昇。広告大手ＷＰＰは５．４％値上がりした。

一方、製薬・バイオテクノロジー株指数は０．４６％安。消費者向けヘルスケア企業ヘイリオンは１５．０％下落。売上高の伸び率見通しを引き下げたことを受け、売りが膨らんだ。

銀行株指数は０．７８％下落。２６年７─９月期決算を発表した英銀大手のロイズは５．０％安。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞

続伸して取引を終えた。欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）による政策金利の据え置き決定を受け、ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種指数は９月８日以来の高値で引けた。堅調な企業業績も相場を支援した。

２０２６年７─９月期決算で純利益が２２年以来の高水準となった石油大手シェルは２．１％上昇。四半期決算で利益が２倍以上となったフランス石油大手トタルは１．２％高。

通期の業績見通しを維持した航空機大手エアバスは２．３％値上がりした。

直近四半期の売上高が増えたドイツの半導体製造装置メーカー、アイクストロンは８．５％高。売上高が市場予想を上回ったフランス自動車大手ルノー・グループは６．９％上昇した。

一方、ＳＴＯＸＸユーロ圏銀行株指数は０．３１％安。四半期決算を発表したスペインの銀行バンコ・ビルバオ・ビスカヤ・アルヘンタリヤ（ＢＢＶＡ）は２．６％下落した。

ＥＣＢは金利を据え置いたものの、エネルギー価格の上昇を受けてインフレリスクが高まっているとして１２月の利上げの可能性に含みを残した。ＥＣＢのラガルド総裁は任期途中で退任することを明らかにした。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞

域内国債利回りが低下した。欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）がこの日の理事会で予想通り政策金利を据え置いた中、市場はＥＣＢが１２月に利上げに踏み切るとの見方を維持した。

ＥＣＢは２９日、予想通り政策金利を据え置くと決定した。ただ、エネルギー価格の急騰を受けてインフレリスクが高まっていると警告し、１２月の利上げの可能性に含みを残した。

また同日、ＥＣＢラガルド総裁は辞意を表明し、総裁の去就を巡る数カ月にわたる臆測に終止符を打った。

市場が織り込む、ＥＣＢが１２月理事会で２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）の利上げを実施する確率は約７５％。また、来年に少なくとももう１回利上げが実施されるとの見方を織り込んでいる。

ユーロ圏の指標金利であるドイツの１０年債利回りは３ｂｐ低下の３．３５％。

ＥＣＢの政策金利見通しに敏感な独２年債利回りは５ｂｐ低下の３．０６％。

フランス１０年債利回りは約１ｂｐ低下の４．９％。独仏１０年債利回り格差は約１５５ｂｐに拡大した。

• OpenAI said the update is part of its AI alignment efforts to help models apply human values in unfamiliar situations, while remaining subject to human oversight • The revised framework says models should minimize harm, be transparent about what they know and do not know, and help users make their own decisions and pursue their own goals • The company said current models do not yet fully reflect the updated Model Spec and that it is exploring new training methods to help models internalize the principles • The move echoes rival Anthropic's Constitutional AI approach, which uses a written "constitution" of principles to guide model behavior and make the values shaping AI systems more transparent • The move follows growing scrutiny of AI alignment after OpenAI disclosed that an autonomous AI agent hacked Hugging Face during testing, a case that highlighted how advanced models can break rules or bypass safeguards while pursuing assigned goals

item.title: Microsoft's cloud growth, cash flow offer respite from AI spending fears
item.description: Microsoft's Azure cloud business grew 48% in the September quarter, while free cash flow reached $18.6 billion, easing investor concerns over mounting AI infrastructure spending.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Microsoft on Wednesday delivered a big cash flow beat and forecast strong cloud growth, offering fresh evidence that its hefty artificial intelligence (AI) bets were paying off even as concerns mount over Big Tech’s spending spree. The results underscore a widening financial divide among the industry's biggest AI spenders, as soaring infrastructure costs force some rivals to turn more heavily to capital markets. Microsoft’s shares rose more than 3 per cent in after-hours trading. The company posted market-beating 48 per cent growth in its Azure cloud business in its fiscal first quarter ended September, and generated $18.6 billion in free cash flow, some $10 billion more than analysts expected. That financial firepower set the firm apart from its rivals such as Alphabet and Meta, whose heavy AI investments have squeezed free cash flow and increased their reliance on borrowing. “Microsoft’s first-quarter report was about as clean as it gets for a company this size,” said Jesse Cohen, senior analyst at Investing.com. “After Meta’s and Alphabet’s numbers revived AI-spending anxiety, this is the counterweight. Demand still exceeds supply, the commercial backlog is enormous, and returns are finally showing up in earnings and overall revenue.” The results also showed Microsoft capitalising on corporate demand for AI, easing fears that the technology threatens its software empire and that its AI fortunes are too closely tied to unprofitable OpenAI. Still, its ties to the AI lab netted it $10 billion in revenue in the September quarter. Microsoft shares have risen about 9 per cent so far this year compared with a 13 per cent rise in the S&P 500 index.

item.title: ドアダッシュ、インスタカートを約170億ドルで買収へ 米食品宅配市場で攻勢
item.description:
Milana Vinn Anuja Bharat Mistry
[２９日 ロイター] - 米料理宅配大手ドアダッシュは...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ドアダッシュ、インスタカートを約170億ドルで買収へ　米食品宅配市場で攻勢 3:19 配信

ドアダッシュの配達用バッグ。米ニューヨーク市ブルックリンで2022年5月撮影。REUTERS/Andrew Kelly（ロイター） Milana Vinn　Anuja Bharat Mistry

[２９日 ロイター] - 米料理宅配大手ドアダッシュは２９日、食料品宅配企業インスタカート（メープルベア）を約１７０億ドルで買収すると発表した。競争が激化する中、成長する米食品配達市場への進出を加速させる。取引は２０２７年末から２８年前半に完了する見込み。

食料品やその他の小売分野に事業を拡大し、大規模な施設や配送網を持つ米小売り大手ウォルマートや通販大手アマゾン・ドット・コムといった資金力のある企業に対抗する狙いがあるとみられる。実現すればドアダッシュにとって過去最大規模となる。料理宅配業界はコスト高や配達員の規制強化もある中で、世界的に業界再編が進んでいる。

ドアダッシュのトニー・シュー共同創業者兼最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は「食料品はオンラインで成功させるのが最も難しい分野の一つ」とし、インスタカートはそのサービスをうまく提供する方法を長年にわたり蓄積してきたと言及した。

ドアダッシュは、インスタカートの株主の保有株１株につき６５ドルを提示。買収報道が出る前の２２日の終値に対して約２６％のプレミアムが付いた水準。

アナリストは、取引完了までの期間が長いことは、双方が長期にわたる反トラスト（独占禁止）審査を見込んでいることを示唆しているとした。

当局への提出書類によると、インスタカートの解約金は６億５０００万ドル。特定の状況で取引が中止された場合、ドアダッシュは１２億５０００万ドルを支払う必要がある。

ロイター 関連リンク コラム：武田薬のシャイアー買収5年、大型Ｍ＆Ａの難しさ示す アングル：中国発ＳＨＥＩＮ、買収主導で増収率の回復狙う アングル：英企業対象のＭ＆Ａ、年初来総額が1920億ドルと記録的な急増 焦点：訂正-焦点：高値の提案も拒否可能、経産省が買収指針明確化　同意なき買収にどう影響 アングル：日本のＭ＆Ａで増す株主の存在感、経営判断の「その後」も意識 10/30(金) 3:19 最終更新 ロイター

item.description: WASHINGTON, Oct 29 : A meteorite found in 2022 in the Sahara in Mali formed in the Martian crust at least 4.1 billion years ago, according to scientists, making the reddish igneous rock perhaps the oldest of the 435 meteorites from Mars known on Earth.The researchers said the composition of the meteorite, cal

Martian meteorite found in the Sahara is 4.1 billion years old

Teghaza 001, a rose-colored rock that is among the oldest Martian meteorites ever found on Earth, in this handout image released on October 29, 2026. Darryl Pitt/Maine Mineral & Gem Museum/via NASA/Handout via REUTERS.

WASHINGTON, Oct 29 : A meteorite found in 2022 in the Sahara in Mali formed in the Martian crust at least 4.1 billion years ago, according to scientists, making the reddish igneous rock perhaps the oldest of the 435 meteorites from Mars known on Earth. The researchers said the composition of the meteorite, called Teghaza 001, is providing insight into the environment early in the history of Earth's planetary neighbor, with fresh evidence of liquid water on the surface that bolsters the notion that primordial Mars may have been conducive to microbial life. Planetary scientist Yang Liu of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California, which is managed by Caltech, called the meteorite "a witness to a time when Mars was likely warmer and wetter than it has been for most of its history." The chemistry of the meteorite, a type of coarse-grained rock called gabbro, shows that it experienced interactions with water when it was slowly cooling and crystallizing in the Martian subsurface. It was part of the Martian crust, the planet's outermost layer, but formed from magma originating at greater depths in the planet's mantle.

Mars is now cold, dry and desolate, but extensive evidence indicates it had water flowing on its surface in the form of rivers, lakes and an ocean in the northern hemisphere billions of years ago. Teghaza 001 was discovered in eight pieces, with the largest chunk about the size of a fist, in the desert roughly 21 miles (34 km) from the Malian village of Bir Chali. Its main minerals are feldspar and pyroxene, and it contains zircon crystals bearing the element uranium. The researchers ascertained its age using a technique based on the decay of uranium into lead over time. "Martian meteorites are our only samples from Mars, forming our basis for understanding the formation and differentiation of early Mars and allowing us to evaluate in laboratories whether ancient Mars could have supported habitable conditions," said Liu, lead author of a study on the meteorite published in the journal Science. "The detailed information we can extract from these meteorite samples complements and validates our exploration of Mars using satellites, landers and rovers," Liu said. This information provides clues about how the evolution of Mars diverged from Earth's when they were in their infancy and life was beginning to take hold on our planet, Liu said. Earth, Mars and the solar system's other planets formed roughly 4.5 billion years ago.     Only three Martian meteorites, including Teghaza 001, date to the planet's early history. One of them, discovered in Antarctica in 1984, was initially assessed as being about 4.5 billion years old but more recently was determined to have a similar age to Teghaza 001. Teghaza 001 likely is the older of the two, according to the new study. WATER WAS PERCOLATING Isotopes, or forms, of the elements oxygen and hydrogen present in the meteorite show that water was percolating down into the planet's deeper crust, as occurs on Earth, and mixing with molten rock from the mantle. "Multiple lines of evidence in Teghaza 001 suggest Mars' surface had water at more than 4.1 billion years ago. This is reflected by hydrogen isotopes in phosphate and oxygen isotopes in minerals and bulk samples," Liu said. Water is considered a key ingredient for life. "The findings lend support to the idea that early Mars had the necessary ingredients and conditions to harbor life, but do not directly answer the question of whether there was life on Mars," said planetary scientist and study co-author Lee Saper of NASA's Ames Research Center and the BAER Institute in California. "The rock is a snapshot in time that shows how a wetter early Mars with a thick atmosphere could have supported habitable conditions but that these conditions were waning rapidly over the first billion years or so of Mars' existence, trending towards its currently dry and inhospitable environment," Saper said. Teghaza 001's chemistry shows it is distinct from the other known Martian meteorites. It may have originated in the southern highlands, possibly from near Hellas Basin, one of the largest Martian impact craters, Liu said. The meteorite has a dramatic backstory. "It was blasted by an impact from the surface of Mars and was flying through space until its path crossed that of Earth. It then entered the atmosphere as a meteor and survived as a meteorite by landing in the Sahara," Liu said. "We do not know when the sample landed on Earth."

Source: Reuters

Oct 29 : Microsoft is planning to raise about $25 billion through its first US investment-grade bond sale in more than nine years, two sources familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday. The bond sale would make Microsoft the latest tech giant to tap into debt markets to fuel its AI ambitions and had gathered more than $100 billion of orders, or over four times the size of the offering, one of the people said, requesting anonymity as the matter was confidential. Bloomberg News first reported the development. The world's largest tech firms have turned to selling bonds and raising equity over the past year to pay for their AI spending spree, a shift in approach for the Silicon Valley giants that have typically relied on their large coffers to fund investments.

Microsoft is selling the debt in as many as 10 tranches, with maturities ranging from 2 to 40 years, Bloomberg reported, adding that no final decision had been made on the offering's size and that it may change according to demand. Wells Fargo, JPMorgan Chase and UBS Group AG are managing the bond offering, according to the report. UBS, Wells Fargo and JPMorgan declined Reuters' requests for comment. Microsoft pointed Reuters to a regulatory filing that confirms the bond sale without disclosing the size of the sale. The report comes just a day after Microsoft CFO Amy Hood told investors on an earnings call that the company would pursue additional sources of funding "when we believe it is attractive to do so", citing the need to preserve its cash flows and financial flexibility. Microsoft shares fell 0.7 per cent in afternoon trading. The company issued an upbeat current-quarter cloud sales outlook after hours on Wednesday. The company expects to keep generating positive free cash flow in its current fiscal year that runs through June 2027 — making it a standout among Big Tech and hyperscaler peers, which have all started burning through cash to fund their data-center buildout. Investors punished rival Alphabet on Wednesday as it burned $9.07 billion in the third quarter, after selling off Meta last week following the Facebook parent's first cash burn in more than a decade.

item.title: Alphabet loses over $500 billion in market value as AI hits Google search
item.description: Alphabet lost over $500 billion in market value as weaker-than-expected search and advertising sales raised concerns over AI's impact on Google's core business and soaring infrastructure costs.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: Alphabet Inc.’s shares fell more than 13%, for its biggest-ever market value wipeout of more than $500 billion, after the company reported disappointing search and advertising sales that reinforced investor concerns about AI’s threat to its core business. The Google parent reported sales, excluding partner payouts, of $111.2 billion for the third quarter, falling short of analysts’ projections. Ad sales from search and other channels — a business line that accounts for roughly half of overall revenue and is critical to financing the massive AI investments — also missed forecasts, growing at the slowest pace in five quarters. The results and share reaction “show us the margin for error when a hyperscaler spending hundreds of billions on the AI infrastructure buildout” posts disappointing results in its core business, JPMorgan analysts including Doug Anmuth said in a note. The shares declined 13% to $281.37, wiping $511 billion from Alphabet’s market value as of 9:35 a.m. in New York. The company’s performance stood in particularly stark contrast to rival Microsoft Corp., which reported growth in its cloud business that surpassed Wall Street’s expectations while keeping its spending in check. Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler said in an earnings call with investors late Wednesday that the growing popularity of AI Mode, a new tab in Google Search, took a toll on the company’s results. AI queries have “lower monetization,” Schindler said, though he noted that the company was optimistic and has plans to bring more ads to that part of the search engine. For years, Google executives have argued that AI chatbots and features won’t cut significantly into its search business. But investors have worried about the impact on the company’s cash cow as consumers turn to rivals ChatGPT, Claude and Google’s own AI features. The pressure is mounting on Alphabet Chief Executive Officer Sundar Pichai to justify the more than $1 trillion that Google is facing in future payments on resources such as data centers, computing and energy to power his AI ambitions. “This quarter feels like a moment of truth for Alphabet: Either Pichai and his team fix the way the company monetizes AI, or the giant risks losing its leadership in several of its core businesses in the near future,” said Thomas Monteiro, senior analyst at Investing.com. “Until Google shows it can charge for AI the way it once charged for search ads,” he said, every capital spending forecast it issues is going to “read less like ambition and more like a bill.” Google’s sprint to build AI infrastructure for both itself and customers has sent the firm’s capital expenditures soaring to record levels. The firm is working to overhaul popular products such as the search engine, YouTube and Gmail with AI. But those efforts have yet to yield the kind of revenue the investors want to see to justify all the spending. Google’s overall services revenue totaled $96.3 billion in the third quarter, below estimates for $98.4 billion. YouTube advertising sales of $11.2 billion also fell below projections. In the meantime, Google’s AI bets are getting even more expensive. By the end of the third quarter, Google’s future commitments to buy resources such as computing power and energy totaled $924 billion. Upcoming obligations such as data-center leases that haven’t yet commenced hit $152 billion, bringing the company’s total future obligations to well over $1 trillion. For the second quarter in a row, the company posted negative free cash flow, something it had, up until now, never seen since going public. “Search still generates the bulk of Alphabet’s cash, and two straight quarters of negative free cash flow show the pure AI math isn’t working right now,” said Anders Bylund, contributing tech analyst at the Motley Fool. Alphabet said in July that capital expenditures will reach as much as $205 billion this year, more than double what it spent last year. AI requires massive amounts of computing power, and Google is racing to build data centers so it can meet demand for AI from consumers, businesses and its own employees. Alphabet’s equity investments also weighed on the company’s bottom line. Those stakes posted an $8.7 billion loss, in large part due to Alphabet’s SpaceX position. That’s a sharp reversal from the gains it saw a year earlier and the windfall in the second quarter that was mainly driven by SpaceX and an investment in a private company that Bloomberg later identified as Anthropic PBC. Its third-quarter net income was $2.12 a share, falling far below Wall Street’s estimate of $2.99. One bright spot in the report was Google Cloud, which is seen as a key gauge of demand for the company’s AI products and hosting services. The division reported sales of $30.7 billion and profit of $11.1 billion, surpassing analyst estimates of $29.1 billion in revenue and $9.8 billion in profit. Among the unit’s biggest customers are startups such as Anthropic that compete with Google in the AI race. “Cloud is booming, but many of its best customers are building assistants that are already beating Google with consumers,” Monteiro wrote. “Right now, Alphabet earns more selling AI to its rivals than using it itself, and that gap should keep growing over the next few quarters unless its models change drastically, and quickly.” Over the past few years, Google has been working to reinvent its search engine for the AI age, trying to keep consumers in the habit of relying on its answers even as chatbots from OpenAI and Anthropic become more popular. The company now delivers AI-generated answers in response to many searches, a shift that has had major implications for businesses that have traditionally relied on the search giant for traffic and advertising revenue. Google has worked particularly hard on building an edge by generating more personalized responses to questions, leveraging years of information about its users. In recent months, though, the company has fallen behind Anthropic and OpenAI in developing AI coding tools. Google recently released Gemini 4, which it says excels in areas such as coding and cybersecurity, though some employees fear the company has yet to fully catch up. Hours before its earnings call, Google announced yet another new AI model known as Carbon, a potential answer to the critics who’ve called for the company to speed up the pace of AI development. “We have more models coming soon,” Pichai told analysts on the call, “including more efficient versions to help developers optimize for speed and cost and to deploy across our billions of users.”

item.description: Oct 29 : Wall Street's top alternative asset managers are betting on the AI boom by owning the infrastructure behind it and locking in rent through long-term leases.With concerns growing that debt-laden neocloud companies at the heart of the AI infrastructure boom could default and that massive spending on th

FAST

Oct 29 : Wall Street's top alternative asset managers are betting on the AI boom by owning the infrastructure behind it and locking in rent through long-term leases. With concerns growing that debt-laden neocloud companies at the heart of the AI infrastructure boom could default and that massive spending on the sector may fail to deliver adequate returns, industry executives are also emphasizing their focus on high-quality, long-term tenants. Blue Owl Co-CEO Marc Lipschultz said the company owns physical infrastructure critical to the growth of the digital economy. "We typically lease it out for 15 to 20 years with annual rent escalators, creating a highly predictable and growing stream of rental income for our investors," Lipschultz said, adding Blue Owl focuses on limiting risks including those tied to short-term leases and token pricing.

Shares of alternative asset managers rose on Thursday, with Blue Owl up 6.5 per cent and Ares Management gaining 2 per cent. KKR and Blackstone each rose 2.5 per cent, while Apollo Global gained 3.7 per cent. THE GREAT AI BUILDOUT Data centers have become a critical part of the AI boom, housing the servers and computing equipment needed to train and run AI models. As the world's biggest technology companies race to expand computing capacity, demand for such facilities has surged, creating what industry executives have described as a generational opportunity for alternative asset managers. Blue Owl said it has more than 130 data centers operating or under construction, representing nearly 14 gigawatts of leased and owned capacity, with another 21 gigawatts in its pipeline. "We are not making a bet on AI when we invest in data centers," Blue Owl CFO Alan Kirshenbaum said, adding that the company does not expect demand for computing power to decline. "We are taking Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, credit risk." Ares Management said its data center development strategy focuses on metropolitan areas including Tokyo, Osaka, London and Sao Paulo, pre-leasing projects to investment-grade hyperscalers under 12- to 15-year leases with no termination rights and inflation escalators. Blackstone last week also highlighted its focus on physical infrastructure and long-term contracted assets. The vast majority of its data center portfolio has initial lease terms of 15 to 20 years, with 96 per cent of counterparties rated investment grade and an average market capitalisation of $2.5 trillion. "So when we think about risk, that doesn't feel particularly risky to us," Blackstone President Jonathan Gray told analysts on a post-earnings call. CAPEX BOOM The AI spending spree across data centers, power, equipment and software is one of the biggest investment waves in history, rivaling those that accompanied the advent of the internet and the expansion of railways. Ares estimates AI-related capex demand at just over $5 trillion through 2030, including roughly $2 trillion for physical data center buildings and adjacent power generation and transmission infrastructure. Asked about the AI selloff earlier this month, Ares CEO Michael Arougheti said investors were becoming more discerning about counterparty risk and how to price it. He also downplayed the impact of higher borrowing costs on AI capex financing, saying the alternative would be to fund projects with equity. "As the capex numbers have continued to scale, they went from largely equity-funded to then high-grade funded and now you're starting to see some of that funding demand flow through into the leveraged finance and private credit market. So there's an evolution here," Arougheti said. Ratings agency Moody's said earlier this week that AI and digital infrastructure were creating large, long-duration financing needs that broaden the private credit market beyond traditional direct lending. "Many borrowers and counterparties are investment grade. However, concentration, construction, residual-value and circular-financing risks are growing," Moody's said.

Source: Reuters

Oct 29 : Eutelsat expects commercial services revenue of more than €10 billion ($11.1 billion) between 2032 and 2040 as it takes a leading role in the European Union's planned alternative to Elon Musk's Starlink satellite internet service, it said on Thursday. The Franco-British operator had been chosen to lead the low Earth orbit (LEO) segment of the EU's IRIS² network that will feature 330 satellites. The first IRIS² satellites are scheduled for launch in 2029, with initial services expected from 2030. Eutelsat has gained prominence as Europe tries to reduce the bloc's reliance on US technology after President Donald Trump's return to office, since it owns OneWeb, the only LEO satellite network alternative to SpaceX's Starlink. In a trading update, the Paris-based company said its backlog now includes €8.9 billion of revenue from designing and building IRIS², to be recognised primarily between 2027 and 2031. That alone is more than seven times the €1.24 billion of revenue Eutelsat generated last year, and lifts its total backlog to €12.1 billion from €3.4 billion at end-June.

The forecast is a major boost for a company aiming to offset its waning video broadcasting business with satellite internet services. OneWeb has more than 600 satellites and 229 more are planned in a €1 billion expansion. Eutelsat said it will invest a combined €3.39 billion in shared and commercial infrastructure on the IRIS² network between 2027 and 2034, in return for access to more than twice OneWeb's current bandwidth. Despite the upbeat outlook, first-quarter revenue fell short of expectations. Revenue from its four operating businesses fell 2.1 per cent like-for-like to €278.3 million in the three months to end-September. That was below the €291 million average of a company-compiled analyst poll. Eutelsat confirmed its financial targets for 2026-27 and 2028-29. ($1 = 0.8971 euros)
